subject: Backup retention exception & cross-border deletion clarifications
messages:

Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying backup purge & deletion scope under the DPA

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great performance on the embedding pipeline. Legal at Acme asked a couple of follow-ups about how backups and logs are treated under the DPA (we're finalizing the SOW). Two asks: 1) When a data deletion request is executed (customer-initiated or DSAR), are backups included in the deletion timeline or treated separately? 2) We operate in multiple jurisdictions and need confirmation on whether copies in backups may be stored in a different region (we need specific language for cross-border retention).

I've attached a short note from our counsel (backup-retention-request.pdf) outlining a proposed carveout: they want a 180-day hold for backups for eDiscovery for healthcare audits. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a temporary retention exception or an amendment to the DPA? If not, what are the technical and procedural constraints?

Appreciate a short write-up we can share with our legal team.

Best,
Jake
Jake O'Neill
Director, Infrastructure
Acme Health

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jake O'Neill <jake.oneill@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying backup purge & deletion scope under the DPA

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Short answer up front: backups are not part of the immediate online deletion path, but they are covered by our DPA and deletion procedures; they are purged on a separate schedule. Below is a concise breakdown you can share with counsel, followed by next steps.

Summary (for counsel):
- Online storage / primary dataset: upon a validated deletion request (DSAR/contractual), we remove customer-identifying data within the standard deletion SLA (typically 30 days), subject to any lawful hold.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots are retained on a separate schedule (default 90 days for hosted accounts). Backups are logically isolated; we treat them as immutable copies for disaster recovery and operational troubleshooting.
- Exceptions for legal hold / eDiscovery: we can implement a documented retention exception; operationally this translates to preventing scheduled purge for the affected tenant identifier for the requested period. An amendment to the DPA or a signed amendment (DocuSign) is recommended to formalize the exception.
- Cross-border: backups may be stored in the region of the replication target; we can provide region scoping per contract. For Acme Health (US region) we will pin backups to US-only storage if required and document subprocessors handling those copies.

Operational constraints & notes:
- Subprocessors: some cloud backups may transit or be handled by our managed-storage subprocessor (listed in the attached subprocessors-current.csv). Any required subprocessor restrictions should be reviewed — we can add specific subprocessor notifications to the DPA amendment.
- Technical feasibility: we can offer a temporary extension to the snapshot retention window (up to 180 days) via a label in our snapshot service; this is non-destructive and reversible. Purge of encrypted backups requires KMS key rotation/zeroization workflows if a deletion is requested. That adds complexity and takes ~72-120 hours per dataset to validate.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will attach the relevant DPA excerpt (see attached DPA_section_7_exported.pdf) that references backups & retention semantics.
2) Kimberly, Marissa — can you confirm operational readiness to apply a 180-day snapshot retention label and flag any billing/ordering changes?
3) Jake — if counsel prefers, we can issue a short DPA amendment and route via DocuSign (I can coordinate).

If helpful, I can also provide a short template clause for the amendment.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Clarifying backup purge & deletion scope under the DPA

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's request. High level: they want a 180-day backup hold for audit/eDiscovery. Operational asks: can we implement a retention label at tenant level that prevents purge of snapshots and backups for that tenant for 180 days? Also need rough T-shirt estimate for effort + any chargeback.

Marissa: can you confirm whether we have existing config toggles for snapshot retention per customer (I recall a plan-based retention but not tenant label)? If not, what's the rollout ETA for a manual exception path?
Karthik: we'll need a short runbook for KMS/key handling if they later request crypto-erasure for backups. Any blockers?

If we can do a low-touch manual retention label we should accept, sign amendment, and bill pro-rata for extended storage. Jake and Acme Legal want this answered by EOD tomorrow.

-K

Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarifying backup purge & deletion scope under the DPA

Kimberly — we have a per-plan snapshot TTL in the control plane today (default 90d for hosted). We also have an internal "retention-exception" label used by CS to pause purges for specific tenants for incident response. It's not surfaced in self-serve yet but we can apply it manually.

Estimate & approach:
- Manual exception path: 2-4 hours for CS/infra to apply label + verify (we'll document the tenant id). No code changes.
- Billing: storage will accrue at standard snapshot rates; recommend a pro-rata monthly charge in the SOW.
- KMS/crypto-erasure: if they request deletion of backups via key-revocation, engineering needs a runbook; Karthik, I suggest we scope 1-2 days to validate for the specific tenant and confirm timelines (we cannot guarantee instantaneous crypto-erasure).

I'll prepare a small PDF (redwood-snapshot-retention-plan.pdf) with the operational steps and estimated costs; Soojin, can you share that with Jake and Legal and offer the DocuSign path?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
